newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM, bankers discuss privatisation of banks.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM, bankers discuss privatisation of banks.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and representatives of the banking sector met on Friday to discuss the sector's privatisation, the government's press office said in a statement.
It said both sides stressed the necessity of further privatisation of banks because "the state cannot be an effective strategic investor in banks.

"The prime minister also stressed the need for an international openness of the Polish banking system and supported the plan of creating strong banking groups with a domination of Polish capital," the statement said.
Under the plan state-owned commercial bank Bank Pekao SA would become the leader of a banking group composed of three other state-owned commercial banks.
So far, of the nine commercial banks carved out of the National Bank of Poland after the fall of communism in 1989, four have been privatised and two are slated for sale this year and next.
The statement also said bankers gave the prime minister a list of postulates concerning the future and shape of the banking system. It gave no further details.
